title: Encrypted DNS Discovery RFC 9463 DNSSEC Policy Architecture
purpose: Define the local DNSSEC validation policy boundary for RFC 9463 ADN-only encrypted DNS discovery.
design_summary: The DNSSEC policy slice keeps live validation outside the DNS package and accepts a caller-supplied DNSSEC validation status for ADN-only SVCB resolution. Secure DNSSEC validation is the only accepted status. Insecure, bogus, indeterminate, or missing validation are rejected so SVCB-derived resolver parameters are not promoted as RFC 9463 active-attack mitigation without DNSSEC proof.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is immutable and side-effect free. It does not perform DNS queries, build DNSSEC chains, manage trust anchors, install host resolvers, or establish encrypted DNS sessions.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Secure DNSSEC validation accepts ADN-only SVCB-derived resolver parameters.
Insecure, bogus, and indeterminate DNSSEC outcomes are rejected.
A missing or not-evaluated DNSSEC status is rejected for ADN-only SVCB resolution.
Self-contained DNR options with addresses and service parameters continue to use the existing RFC 9463 discovery path and do not depend on this ADN-only SVCB policy.
risks: This slice trusts the caller-supplied DNSSEC validation status.
This slice does not implement a validating resolver, DNSSEC chain construction, live SVCB querying, or platform resolver installation.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The boundary turns the RFC 9463 DNSSEC mitigation note into deterministic local policy without coupling Incursa.Quic.Dns to a DNSSEC resolver stack or operating-system resolver adapter.
